gen_risks.description: Training institutions lack adequate equipment, infrastructure and staff, risking delayed or low‑quality delivery of market‑aligned courses.
gen_risks.mitigation: Phase upgrades, procure modern equipment, fund staff recruitment and training, and monitor capacity against a standardized checklist.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 12: capacity constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps.

gen_risks.description: Geographic isolation of Príncipe may hinder construction logistics and beneficiary access to the new training centre.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop detailed transport plans, use local contractors, and provide remote‑learning modules and transport subsidies for participants.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 30: Príncipe’s geographic isolation and limited skilled‑worker pool constrain diversification and growth.

gen_risks.description: Increased frequency of floods, storms and landslides could disrupt construction and training activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply climate‑resilient design (EDGE, rainwater harvesting), install backup generators, and schedule works outside peak hazard periods.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 4 & 61: STP vulnerable to coastal floods, storms, landslides; climate events may disrupt service delivery.

gen_risks.description: Delays in recording financial transactions and internal audits may weaken fiduciary controls.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint an experienced accountant, customize the accounting system for timely reporting, and enforce quarterly audit reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 56: FM risks include delays in recording transactions and internal audit reviews.

gen_risks.description: Procurement may be slowed if AFAP and ministries fail to coordinate technical specifications and evaluation committees.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish joint procurement task‑forces, finalize TORs early, and set clear timelines for evaluation panels.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 57: procurement performance depends on close collaboration between AFAP and MLSSS.

gen_risks.description: Only 6 % of youth are enrolled in TVET, limiting the pool of participants for the project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Intensive outreach, scholarships covering transport/accommodation, and partnerships with schools to raise awareness and enrollment.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 12: Only six percent of STP’s youth are currently enrolled in TVET.

gen_risks.description: Female participants may face gender‑based violence or sexual exploitation during training or internships.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire GBV/SEA specialist, enforce strict codes of conduct, provide safe facilities and grievance mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenants: AFAP must hire a Social Specialist with GBV/SEA expertise.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private‑sector commitment could limit apprenticeship slots and on‑the‑job training opportunities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create Workforce Development Committees, offer performance‑based compensation to firms, and set minimum placement targets.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 27: Employers engaged via Workforce Development Committees and partial compensation based on student numbers.

gen_risks.description: Failure to meet IDA disbursement conditions could postpone fund releases.
gen_risks.mitigation: Track all pre‑conditions, submit required reports on schedule, and maintain a compliance checklist.
gen_risks.evidence: Conditions section: Disbursement requires execution of Sub‑Grant forms and payment agent hiring.

gen_risks.description: The new labor‑market information system may remain under‑utilized, reducing its impact on employment services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide intensive staff training, integrate system with existing databases, and set usage KPIs linked to funding.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 32: Employment Observatory never fully operationalized; new system to be cloud‑based.

gen_risks.description: The Contingent Emergency Response Component manual might be delayed, limiting rapid response to crises.
gen_risks.mitigation: Draft the CERC manual during project set‑up, obtain early approval, and train staff on activation procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 47: CERC manual to be prepared and adopted after project effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Risk of elite capture or exclusion of the most vulnerable if targeting criteria are not transparent.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use USR data for objective selection, publish criteria, and monitor grievance redress outcomes.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 59: Risks of exclusion and elite capture if benefits not equitably distributed.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑smart curricula may not be adopted by firms, limiting relevance of training.
gen_risks.mitigation: Involve employers in curriculum design via Workforce Development Committees and conduct post‑training adoption surveys.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 27: Committees will identify skills gaps, including climate‑smart agriculture.

gen_risks.description: Low uptake of labor‑mobility information could reduce migration‑linked job opportunities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Promote the Employability Portal, partner with overseas employers, and run information campaigns on safe migration.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 24: Labor mobility approach includes portal and partnerships with destination employers.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient monitoring and evaluation capacity may lead to poor data quality and limited learning.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire Data/IT assistant, conduct regular data audits, and provide M&E training to PIU staff.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenants: AFAP must hire a Data/IT assistant within 60 days of effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Political or administrative changes in ministries could affect project governance and continuity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalize the coordination committee with clear terms of reference and maintain regular ministerial briefings.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 49: Coordination committee established under authority of the Minister of Labor.

gen_risks.description: Severe weather events could damage the new training centre on Príncipe, causing cost overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply EDGE certification, incorporate flood‑resilient design, and secure appropriate construction insurance.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 31: Construction will meet EDGE standards and include climate‑resilient design.

gen_risks.description: Limited private‑sector capacity may not absorb all trained youth, leading to unemployment after training.
gen_risks.mitigation: Scale self‑employment grants, entrepreneurship boosters, and linkages to export markets to create alternative jobs.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 3: Economy dominated by few medium/large firms; MSMEs are 92 % but low‑productivity.

gen_risks.description: Corruption or fraud in procurement and grant disbursement could erode project credibility and funds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce World Bank procurement rules, conduct independent audits, and publish procurement outcomes publicly.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 57: Procurement to follow World Bank regulations and anti‑fraud guidelines.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient digital connectivity may limit use of the Employability Portal and data systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Invest in connectivity upgrades, provide backup power, and test portal performance before rollout.
gen_risks.evidence: Section 28: Physical investments include connectivity upgrades to enable access to digital technologies.

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
